title: Telemetry prioritization canvas and heuristics
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a lightweight decision canvas for telemetry prioritization across inference runtime components (serving runtime, KV cache, routing/fallbacks, batching). The goal is to give product and infra teams a repeatable heuristic for: 1) which signals to instrument first, 2) how to budget dashboard real estate, and 3) an initial sampling/tracing strategy that preserves investigatability without exploding cost.

Audience:
- Observability engineers
- SREs and runtime infra
- Feature owners launching model rollouts or routing changes

How to use this canvas (quick):
1) Pick the user-facing scenario (e.g., canary rollout of quantized model; tenant cold-cache spike)
2) Walk through the decision checklist below and mark "must-have / nice-to-have / postpone" for each signal
3) Capture owners, example queries, dashboard widgets, and sampling knobs in the rollout ticket
4) Revisit after 2 weeks of live traffic to prune or promote signals based on incidence and cost

Decision checklist (heuristics):
- Severity-first: instrument anything that is a 1– or 2–blast user-impact (hard failure, 95th/99th latency breaches). Must-have.
- Actionability: prefer signals that produce a clear next action (evict, throttle, rollback, warm cache). Must-have for runbooks.
- SNR (signal-to-noise): prefer metrics with stable baseline and clear delta on regressions. If a metric is noisy, add tags/cohorts before promoting.
- Cost-to-value: estimate query cost for dashboards and traces. If a metric needs frequent (every 15s) recompute across all tenants and costs >2x budget, consider aggregated alternatives (percentiles, sampled probes).
- Ownership alignment: signals without owners are postponed. Always assign primary and fallback owners.

Prioritization matrix (quick guide):
- Tier 0 (immediate): 99th latency per model, error rate (per endpoint), SLO burn, tenant cold-cache ratio, model fallback count
- Tier 1 (soon): prefix hit ratio, batching-size distribution, KV cache miss latency, per-tenant token cost
- Tier 2 (later): fine-grained operator-level timings, micro-op kernel counters, distribution of attention memory usage (heavy instrumentation, large cardinality)

Metric definitions (examples to drop into tickets):
- request.latency_ms.p99: 99th percentile of end-to-end request latency measured at API ingress (include routing time + model generation). Query hint: histograms aggregated by 10ms buckets.
- model.fallback.count: counter of requests where a fallback model was used due to capacity or error. Tag by reason: capacity|error|healthcheck.
- kvcache.prefix_hit_rate: ratio of requests that reused prefix entries from KV cache within the same session. Backfill window: last 30m.
- batching.opportunity_ratio: fraction of requests in a 1s window that could have been batched given model sequence length similarity threshold (configurable).

Trace anchoring and span recommendations:
- Top-level span: request_id, tenant_id, route, selected_model, selected_variant, routing_policy
- Model span: include model_name, quantization_profile, kernel_path, sequence_length, kvcache_used (bool)
- Batch span: batch_size, composition (homogeneous|mixed), batching_delay_ms
- Error span: include error_code, upstream_error, retry_attempts, fallback_trigger
- Use semantic attributes instead of long text fields for reasons (reason:capacity|temperature|memory) to make querying fast.

Adaptive sampling guidance:
- Baseline: deterministic sampling of 0.5% of successful requests, 100% of errors, 2% of high-latency (>p95) requests.
- Canary/rollout mode: increase sampling to 5–10% for both errors and p95+ requests for the duration of the canary window.
- Tenant-weighted: for enterprise tenants with SLAs, override and always sample at 100% for that tenant_id.
- Trace enrichment: sampled traces should capture a bounded-sized payload of the prompt (first 1k chars) + model logits summary. Redact PII by default.

Dashboard and widget budget rules:
- Dashboard cardinality cap: keep dashboards <12 widgets where possible. If a product needs >12, split into scoped tabs (eg: "runtime overview", "cost lens", "tenant anomalies").
- Widget cost label: annotate widget with estimated query cost (Low|Medium|High) and refresh interval. Default refreshs: Low=60s, Medium=30s, High=15s.
- Cohort-first widgets: prefer cohorted percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for tenant slices rather than raw top-N lists which are expensive.
- Alert anchoring: every alert should map to one runbook action and one dashboard widget. If not, lower alert severity until clarified.

Investigation playbook (operator flow):
1) Observe alert or user report
2) Open the tempo probe (synthetic probe) for affected model/route to validate reproducibility
3) Check request.latency_ms.p99 and model.fallback.count for the last 15m
4) If fallback spikes, inspect routing decisions and capacity metrics (node.gpu_utilization, pool.available_slots)
5) If latency spikes without fallback, examine kvcache.prefix_hit_rate and batching.opportunity_ratio
6) If traces needed, kick off higher-sample traces for the affected tenant (temporary increase) and attach trace to incident
7) Post-mortem: record whether a new metric or trace attribute would have shortened time-to-detect; add to backlog with priority by this canvas

Example queries (PromQL / pseudo):
- p99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
- fallback rate: sum(increase(model_fallback_count[15m])) by (model, reason) / sum(increase(requests_total[15m])) by (model)
- kv prefix hit: sum(increase(kvcache_prefix_hits[30m])) / sum(increase(kvcache_prefix_lookups[30m]))

Runbooks and ownership template (to paste into rollout ticket):
- Primary owner: <team/person>
- On-call escalation: eng-sre -> infra-runtime -> applied-ml
- SLOs impacted: list SLO ids and current burn rate query
- Quick mitigation steps: 1) enable fallback to warmed variant 2) throttle low-priority tenants 3) scale pool by x nodes 4) revert rollout

Open questions / tradeoffs to decide in ticket:
- How much of prompt payload can we include in traces without violating cost/compliance? Draft limit: 1k characters redacted.
- Should we keep a permanent 1% tail trace sample for all tenants for historical debugging vs. the cost hit?
- Metric partitioning: per-tenant p99 is expensive—prefer percentile bucketing with tenant-weighted probes vs full aggregation.

Next steps for pilots (2-week plan):
- Week 0: pick 2 feature rollouts and apply canvas; instrument Tier 0 signals and add basic dashboard widgets (p99, fallback, kv hit)
- Week 1: enable adaptive sampling and add trace enrichment policy for canaries
- Week 2: review cost and utility; prune widgets marked "postpone" and promote one Tier 1 signal if a gap is found

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Build a lightweight "widget-cost" label generator in the dashboard provisioning script
- Add a small SQL snippet library for common debug queries and attach to runbook template
- Schedule a 60-minute working session with applied-ml and infra to agree on trace attribute set

Appendix: short definitions and why they matter:
- kvcache.prefix_hit_rate: high impact on user latency for multi-turn chat; low cardinality if we bucket by session-age
- model.fallback.count: critical indicator of capacity stress and primary signal for tenant experience regressions
- batching.opportunity_ratio: helps trade off latency vs cost (higher batching reduces token cost but increases tail latency)

If you want, I can extract the checklist into a simple Confluence template and a dashboard manifest for the first two pilot rollouts.
